title: Argentine artist Nicola Costantino opens a solo exhibition at L'Space Gallery
summary: L’SPACE Gallery presents Where Time Stands Still, a solo exhibition by internationally acclaimed Argentine artist Nicola Costantino on view November 5 - December 19, 2026. A leading figure in contemporary Latin American art, Costantino is known for her provocative and multidisciplinary practice, which has challenged conventional ideas of beauty, identity, desire, and the human body for more than three decades. She represented Argentina at the 2013 Venice Biennale, and her work is held in the collection of the Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), New York. In this new chapter of her practice, Costantino turns toward beauty itself as a form of provocation. Far from being merely decorative or reassuring, beauty can be unsettling, disturbing, and even threatening. title: The Cleveland Museum of Art acquires transformational collection of early photography of China
summary: The Cleveland Museum of Art (CMA) today announced the acquisition of 734 photographs of China dating from the 1850s through the early 1920s. Acquired from the collection of rare book and photography dealer Stephan Loewentheil, the group includes approximately 400 works by 16 Chinese photographers alongside more than 300 photographs by British and European practitioners, along with a small number of American and Japanese photographers, bringing together Chinese and Western perspectives on a period of profound cultural, political, and social transformation. title: Cigar store Indian figure attributed to the shop of Samuel Robb topped a list of high-fliers at Morphy's
summary: A late-19th-century cigar store Indian figure attributed to the shop of Samuel Robb (American, 1851-1928) rose to $60,000, and a Mosler Safe Company (Hamilton, Ohio) “Cannonball” salesman’s sample safe brought $56,580 to dominate prices realized at Morphy’s October 16-17 Coin-Op & Advertising Auction. The much-anticipated event was held at Morphy’s West Coast satellite gallery in Las Vegas, Nevada. The auction included more than 1,100 lots of rare, high-quality antiques and vintage collectibles. title: Vietnamese Modernists Join Gauguin, Claudel and Dürer in Heritage's Nov. 19 European Art Auction
summary: Seven paintings by Lê Phô trace a remarkable artistic journey, from intimate flowers painted on silk to exuberant blooms rendered in richly worked oil. Together with Vu Cao Dam’s dreamlike image of a musician, they form the heart of an eight-work offering of Vietnamese modernism in Heritage’s Nov. 19 European Art Signature® Auction. The group joins works by Paul Gauguin, Camille Claudel, Albrecht Dürer, Bartolomeo Passerotti and John Constable in a sale that rewards close looking across five centuries of art. “This group offers collectors a wonderful opportunity to follow Lê Phô’s development across several decades and to see his work in conversation with Vu Cao Dam’s,” says Marianne Berardi, Heritage’s Co-Director of European

title: Stedelijk Museum announces major Yayoi Kusama retrospective
summary: The Stedelijk Museum is presenting a landmark retrospective of Yayoi Kusama, one of the most influential and pioneering artists of the 20th and 21st centuries. This expansive exhibition explores more than seven decades of Kusama’s groundbreaking work. The exhibition delves into the wide range of artistic media Kusama has worked with over the years, including painting, sculpture, installations, drawing, fashion, collage, happenings, and more. Yayoi Kusama (1929 - 2026) is internationally renowned for her exploration of themes such as infinity, self-obliteration, and repetition. Her distinctive use of polka dots, mirror rooms, and immersive installations has become emblematic of her artistic vision. Kusama’s work invites viewers into dynamic environments that blur the boundaries between the observer and the infinite, challenging perceptions of space and the self. title: Gagosian to present Roy Lichtenstein solo booth at Frieze Abu Dhabi
summary: Gagosian will participate in Frieze Abu Dhabi with a solo presentation of sculptures, prints, drawings, and collages produced by Roy Lichtenstein between 1965 and 1995. This coincides with Roy Lichtenstein: Like New, a major retrospective that opened at the Whitney Museum of American Art, New York, on October 11. In the Abu Dhabi presentation, portraits, landscapes, interiors, and still life compositions reinforce the essential role of work on paper in the American Pop art progenitor’s oeuvre. These works offer an array of characteristically witty and arresting images that together form an index to their maker’s thematic preoccupations and unmistakable visual language. Through series of drawings and prints in particular, Lichtenstein alludes to art historical styles, establishing sequences within which conventional representation shifts gradually toward more abstract interpretation. title: Dorotheum announces Contemporary Week sales featuring over 550 modern and postwar works
summary: Dorotheum's fourth major auction week of the year is set to feature a stellar roster of renowned artists: Spanning from masterpieces of Viennese Modernism to the leading figures of international postwar and contemporary art, the Contemporary Week runs from 17 November to 3 December 2026. The highlights include a painting by Max Oppenheimer that had been lost since 1935, two newly discovered drawings by Gustav Klimt, works by Egon Schiele and Alfons Walde, as well as international artists such as Ad Reinhardt, Allen Jones, Victor Vasarely, Giorgio de Chirico, and Daniel Richter. Around 550 works of art will be up for auction. After more than nine decades in private hands, appearing at auction for the first time On 17 November 2026, a major work by Max Oppenheimer—his very first depiction of musicians—will hit the block at the Modern Art auction. title: First New York solo presentation of Italian sculptor Leoncillo in over three decades opens at Lévy Gorvy Dayan
summary: Presented in collaboration with Galleria dello Scudo, Lévy Gorvy Dayan will open Leoncillo and the Soul of Clay on November 4, 2026, at 19 East 64th Street, New York. The exhibition will mark the first solo presentation of the artist in New York in more than three decades. Focusing on the radical body of sculpture Leoncillo created in the last ten years of his life from the late 1950s to the 1960s, the presentation honors the artist's singular relationship to the ceramic medium—revealing how clay and terracotta acted not only as Leoncillo's primary materials, but also as an eternal extension of the artist himself. Among the most significant sculptors of the twentieth century, Leoncillo Leonardi—known as Leoncillo—worked with clay from childhood to his earliest days as an artist. title: Galleria Continua presents Sislej Xhafa solo exhibition 'L'eau sans rivière'
summary: GALLERIA CONTINUA / Les Moulins presents L’eau sans rivière, a solo exhibition by Sislej Xhafa bringing together works created over more than two decades of artistic practice, new works conceived specifically for the occasion, and Le Village de l’Imagination, a project developed with children and young people from the local community. L’eau sans rivière unfolds as an exhibition in a constant state of transformation. Existing works, new productions, collective experiments and performances coexist within a shared environment, allowing the exhibition to evolve through the presence and participation of those who inhabit it. At the heart of the exhibition is Le Village de l’Imagination. Over the course of several weeks, children and young people aged 5 to 17 are invited to draw, paint, build, write, move, play and perform. title: Mennour presents Yinka Shonibare's Paris solo debut 'The Wind, the Earth and the Fire'
summary: Mennour is presenting Yinka Shonibare’s first solo exhibition in Paris entitled “The Wind, the Earth and the Fire” at 5 rue du Pont de Lodi. The show brings various ongoing bodies of work into dialogue, including new quilts, hand-painted bronze and textile sculptures, and positions the multidisciplinary artist as one of the leading voices to explore postcolonialism and hybridity in contemporary art. Born in London, raised in Lagos, Nigeria, Shonibare has always experienced the world by navigating, and somehow bridging, distinct cultures. Decolonial studies continue to show how defining a sense of identity and belonging is far more complex than solely relying on what can be found in a national archive. By tracing the history of Dutch wax textiles, Shonibare uncovers the deep layers of complexity embedded within them and conveys the impossibility of pinning down an artifact as authentic. title: The RISD Museum celebrates 150 years of collecting, teaching, and making
summary: In 2027, Rhode Island School of Design and the RISD Museum will celebrate 150 years in Providence. From the beginning, the museum has been an integral part of RISD’s educational mission, providing students with direct access to works of art and design and creating a resource for teaching, learning, research, and creative discovery. Over the past century and a half, both the college and museum have evolved, along with the communities, artists, educators, and ideas that have shaped them. As part of RISD’s 150th anniversary celebration, the RISD Museum will mark this shared milestone through a yearlong program of exhibitions, publications, scholarship, artist projects, and gatherings that explore the museum’s particular history and its continuing role within RISD, Providence, and the broader arts community. title: Colnaghi Madrid announces highlights for FERIARTE 2026
summary: Colnaghi Madrid announced its participation in FERIARTE 2026, where it will present a selection of paintings and sculpture dating from the sixteenth to the early twentieth century, tracing the varied forms of religious, dynastic and domestic image-making across Spain and its overseas territories. Highlights include Juan Bautista Martínez del Mazo's pair of full-length portraits, Portrait of King Philip IV of Spain in Hunting Dress and Portrait of Cardinal-Infante Don Fernando of Austria in Hunting Dress, each nearly two metres high. The paintings bring together brothers whose lives placed them at the centre of Habsburg court and military history. Philip IV, king from 1621 to 1665, was a major patron of the arts and of Diego Velázquez, Mazo's father-in-law and principal artistic model. Don Fernando was appointed cardinal and Archbishop of Toledo at the age of ten, but went on to serve the monarchy as a soldier and governor. title: Fondazione Prada presents major research exhibition 'Global Antiquity' in Milan
summary: Fondazione Prada presents "Global Antiquity," a research exhibition curated by Salvatore Settis, Anna Anguissola, and Chiara Ballestrazzi and designed by Rem Koolhaas and AMO/OMA, in its Milan venue from 5 November 2026 to 1 March 2027 (press preview: Wednesday, 4 November). "Global Antiquity" offers an unprecedented perspective on the interactions between the cultures of the Mediterranean and those of Asia over a broad timespan, from approximately 600 BC to 1000 AD. The exhibition is part of a wider investigation undertaken by Fondazione Prada since 2015, when it simultaneously presented "Serial Classic" and "Portable Classic" in its Milan and Venice spaces, two exhibitions curated by Salvatore Settis (with Anna Anguissola in Milan, and Davide Gasparotto in Venice). title: RAF Museum exhibition brings local people together to explore Barnet's unique heritage
summary: The Royal Air Force Museum London is celebrating the rich history and vibrant communities of Barnet with a new exhibition that brings together aviation heritage, local memories and contemporary art. From Barnet With Love, running from 30 October 2026 to 22 February 2027, explores the borough's past, present and future through a collection of postcards created by local residents, alongside historic images and innovative augmented reality technology. The exhibition is part of Light + Flight, a borough-wide cultural programme presented by Art in Barnet, Barnet Council's arts and culture initiative, celebrating the area's heritage, creativity and communities. title: RM Sotheby's achieves highest ever grossing UK car auction with £36.5 million London sale
summary: RM Sotheby’s London sale achieved total sales £36,550,950, making it the highest grossing UK collector car sale of all time. Held at London’s prestigious Peninsula Hotel in partnership with The Royal Automobile Club and the London to Brighton Veteran Car Run, a remarkable selection of car and memorabilia lots were sold in a packed auction room, with 87.5% of all lots offered successfully sold. The top ten sellers all achieved prices in excess of £1,000,000. The incredible 2022 Daytona SP3 proved to be the top seller, achieving an excellent £8,161,259. The SP3 is unquestionably one the most desirable Ferraris ever created, and the car sold was a designated development car was retained by Ferrari SpA to fulfil an important role as the company’s factory press car, featuring in many important media reviews and an episode BBC’s Top Gear. title: Fotografiska Berlin spotlights Korean-born, Berlin-based artist Miji Ih
summary: In 2020, the Ari Statue of Peace was installed in Berlin's Moabit neighborhood. It was intended to commemorate the so-called "comfort women" across the Asia-Pacific region, who were forced into sexual slavery by the Japanese military during World War II. The statue also honored the courage of survivors who broke decades of silence about their experiences. Its installation prompted protests from the Japanese government and sparked a broad public debate about how the "comfort women" are remembered. For Miji Ih, the Statue of Peace became the starting point for her engagement with the so-called "comfort women," culminating in Mouths: On Water and Whisky, which connects their history with the lived realities of women around U.S. military bases in Japan, South Korea, and Germany. title: Crow Museum of Asian Art presents Japanese bamboo survey with Thoma Foundation
summary: A centuries-old tradition of weaving and shaping bamboo takes striking contemporary form in Twisted, Plaited, Sculpted: Collection of the Carl & Marilynn Thoma Foundation, opening Nov. 7, 2026, and continuing through Oct. 17, 2027, at the Crow Museum of Asian Art’s Dallas Arts District location. Marking the Crow Museum’s first collaboration with the Dallas-based Carl & Marilynn Thoma Foundation, Twisted, Plaited, Sculpted brings together 22 works by 17 Japanese artists, including Living National Treasures Fujinuma Noboru and Fujitsuka Shosei. Drawn from one of the foundation’s four major collecting areas, the exhibition showcases the remarkable breadth and creative possibilities of woven bamboo as artists reshape and manipulate a familiar plant material to push the boundaries of natural form. title: Tony Cokes brings text and music installation to Art Institute of Chicago's Bluhm Family Terrace
summary: The Art Institute of Chicago is presenting Tony Cokes: On Boredom, open now through March 14, 2027. This is Tony Cokes’s first public outdoor presentation in Chicago, and brings his signature style to Bluhm Family Terrace. For over forty years, Cokes has remixed various media sources into vibrant videos, signs, lightboxes, and billboards that are often set to music. His ability to recontextualize fragments of contemporary culture into works and installations that speak directly to the present has made him one of the most celebrated artists working today. title: Walker Art Gallery to present an exhibition of new paintings by 2025 John Moores Painting Prize winner Ally Fallon
summary: Walker Art Gallery, part of National Museums Liverpool, will present Ally Fallon: The Shape of a Room, a solo exhibition of new paintings by the youngest artist ever to win the John Moores Painting Prize, from 14 November 2026 to 16 May 2027. Fallon (b. 1998, London) moved to Manchester to study English literature, with painting taking centre stage in his practice during lockdown. He went on to complete an MA in Painting at Manchester School of Art and was working as a teacher when he won the John Moores Painting Prize in September 2025, aged 27. title: Kunsthaus Biel presents Switzerland's first museum exhibition of Chicanx art
summary: For the first time in Switzerland, «Los Four & Friends» presents an exhibition of Chicanx art in a museum. It showcases the artistic production of Los Four, a Chicano art collective active in California between 1973 and 1984. Centring the history of the collective, the exhibition expands into an exploration of Chicanx art in Los Angeles, from the 1970s to the present. «Chicano», «Chicana» or «Chicanx¹» is a self-defined identity adopted by people of Mexican descent in the United States. Reclaimed during the 1960s Chicano civil rights movement («El Movimiento»), the term became a political and cultural expression of pride in Mexican heritage and a resistance to discrimination. «El Movimiento» fought for economic justice, political representation, educational reform, and the reclamation of Mexican-American identity. title: Palais de Tokyo presents Valérie John's indigo-driven survey 'So Black It Turns Blue'
summary: Valérie John proposes to explore indigo blue as a material, a memory and a gesture. From Martinique to West Africa, her œuvre brings together identities and stories in assemblages that constitute sensory traces of the past. Entitled “I telman nwè ki i blé (So Black It Turns Blue)”, this exhibition presents a selection of Valérie John’s work dating back to the 1990s and her return to Martinique, where she set up a “workshop-work-of-art”. This choice was a commitment to pursuing her œuvre through an immersion in her milieu, one rooted in the island’s translocal memory and in a shifting gesture of identity construction. At the Palais de Tokyo, she proposes an immersion in indigo and its metamorphoses, from the deepest blues to the brightest blacks. title: Marc Selwyn Fine Art opens an exhibition of paintings by Alberto Valdés
summary: Marc Selwyn Fine Art presents an exhibition of paintings by Alberto Valdés, whose work brings ancient Mesoamerican imagery into dialogue with mid-century modernism. Drawing on his Mexican-American heritage, Valdés' evocative figurative and abstract compositions explore history, mysticism, and the natural world. A Beginning reveals a deeply personal vision shaped by ancestral memory and modern experimentation. Alberto Valdés belongs to a generation of Mexican-American artists whose mid-20th century practices predated - yet were intrinsically connected to - El Movimiento, the Chicana/o movement for social justice that gained momentum across the United States during the Vietnam War era. title: Gagosian Beverly Hills presents major survey 'Richard Avedon: Hollywood'
summary: Gagosian is presenting Richard Avedon: Hollywood, an exhibition of more than 120 photographs spanning Avedon’s career of over half a century and including some of his most iconic portraits alongside rarely seen images. The exhibition represents Hollywood as a profoundly American construct whose glamour and power have made it a global cultural touchstone. Opening at the Beverly Hills gallery on November 4, 2026, the presentation is curated by the Richard Avedon Foundation. In the summer of 1956, Avedon was in Paris consulting for Funny Face, the 1957 musical directed by Stanley Donen and starring Audrey Hepburn and Fred Astaire that was loosely based on Avedon’s own improbable life as a young photographer. title: Farah Al Qasimi debuts new photographs and vinyl works at François Ghebaly Beverly Hills
summary: François Ghebaly presents Rubberneck, Farah Al Qasimi’s second solo exhibition at the gallery and first presentation at the Beverly Hills location. Rubberneck opens ahead of Al Qasimi’s forthcoming institutional solo exhibition at the Whitney Museum of American Art in January 2027. Farah Al Qasimi creates films, photographs, and installations that catch on the unmistakable idioms of contemporary life. Drawing from a wellspring of visual touchstones, Al Qasimi’s images place the symbols and symptoms of globalization, cultural dissemination, nationalism, and the online in unexpected arenas of daily life. Her newest exhibition, Rubberneck, brings together 15 new photographs alongside vinyl interventions.
